AUTOMATION
Ask one question across your growth stack.

Three platforms, one answer, and the source figures attached. Reporting and investigation first — every account change is held for a decision.

The questions it answers

›
What changed in spend, ad earnings and subscription revenue last week?

One brief across all three sources, with the periods and currencies reconciled and the joins that do not exist called out.

›
Why did estimated earnings drop on Tuesday?

Broken down through impressions, eCPM, match rate, country, app and ad unit until the change has a named cause.

›
Which campaigns moved after the paywall change?

Campaign reporting beside subscription events, with an explicit statement of what attribution can and cannot support.

How one investigation runs
01
Connect

Named accounts only, with access you grant and can revoke. Restrictions are enforced in the tools, not in an instruction.

02
Validate

Dates, currencies, account mappings and data freshness are checked before a single number is quoted.

03
Explain

A written finding with the source figures attached — and the unknowns named, rather than smoothed over.

04
Propose

Any supported change is presented for approval. Nothing touches an account without a decision behind it.

05
Record

What was changed, by whom, and what happened afterwards. The part that makes the next investigation faster.

Stages 01 to 03 run on read access alone. Stage 04 is the only one that can touch an account, and it does not proceed without a named approval.

What each platform actually supports

Checked against the providers’ own documentation. The boundaries are limits, not a roadmap.

PLATFORM	WHAT WE CAN DO TODAY	THE BOUNDARY
Google Ads	Account discovery, campaign and asset reporting, budget and status inspection, and GAQL queries, through the official MCP server.	Read-only. It cannot change bids, pause campaigns or create assets — those need a separately authorised API path with its own approval record.
AdMob	Apps, ad units and mediation groups, plus network and mediation reporting — impressions, eCPM, match rate and estimated earnings by country, app and ad unit.	Through an audited adapter over the documented REST API. There is no official Google-maintained MCP server for AdMob, and each management operation is validated individually before it is offered.
RevenueCat	Projects, products, offerings and subscription analytics through the official hosted MCP server — trials, renewals, refunds and billing issues.	It also exposes configuration changes. Only the tools a given engagement needs are enabled, scoped to named projects.
The arithmetic nobody checks

Google Ads conversion value often already represents revenue that also appears in RevenueCat or in ad earnings. Summing the dashboards double-counts it. And a shared date or country is not an attribution key: without impression-level revenue or an MMP join, the honest output is an aggregate comparison and a stated limitation, not a ROAS figure.

This is the most common way a cross-source revenue report is wrong, and it is also the argument for having someone do it properly. A number that cannot be supported is not reported as a number.

What it needs from you
Google Ads
Read access to the named customer IDs, through your MCC or a direct grant.
AdMob
API access to the publisher account, scoped to reporting.
RevenueCat
A project-scoped key with only the tools an engagement needs enabled.
Definitions
Your reporting timezone and currency, and which app maps to which Ads customer, AdMob app and RevenueCat project.

Access is granted to named accounts, held by us as the operator, and revocable by you at any time. Restrictions are enforced in the tools and the backend, not by instructing a model to stay inside them. There is no self-serve connection here — this is a consulting engagement, not a portal.
